solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Responsible prisoner's time — out of practice!

parts.note: skills that are out of practice have gone rusty

explanation.surface: A trusted inmate has been away from his work so long he has lost his touch.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of prisoner's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In prison slang a trusted inmate given privileges and light duties is called by this noun.

clue.text: A mist swirling around tabloid catastrophes

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters go round the tabloid
swirling means the letters of a mist spin into a new order

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: Fog swirls about a gutter newspaper covering disasters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' makes TAMIS from A MIST, and 'around' puts SUN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant sea waves that flood coasts are among the worst natural disasters.

clue.text: Stimulant that's found in shoe

definitions.meaning: an informal word for an amphetamine or similar pep pill
the part of a shoe above the sole

explanation.surface: A drug smuggled in footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a stimulant pill and also names the top part of a shoe.

clue.text: Stress formerly missing from new part of house

indicators.note: missing from means the second piece is removed from the first

parts.note: an extension is a new part added to a house
ex means formerly, as in ex-wife

explanation.surface: Worry over building work, once lacking a home extension.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension is mental or physical strain, a synonym for stress.

clue.text: Story about a ship's dog in pictures

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the story goes around the other letters

parts.note: a story can be a lie, a tale that is untrue
SS, steamship, is the usual abbreviation placed before a ship's name

explanation.surface: A tale concerning a vessel's canine appears on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous collie of films and television is the best-known screen dog of all.

clue.text: Important I guarantee to provide accommodation for holiday destination

indicators.note: to provide accommodation for says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hotelier promises to house holidaymakers at their chosen resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is a Caribbean island popular with tourists, an example of a holiday spot.

clue.text: Air pocket occurring mid-flight?

parts.note: a flight is also a set of stairs, and the open shaft around them is an air-filled space

explanation.surface: Turbulence felt by an aircraft halfway through a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: The vertical space that a staircase climbs through is a pocket of air in the middle of the flights.

clue.text: Quote by divorcee to cause great emotion

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: a divorcee is someone's ex
to quote a source is to cite it

explanation.surface: A quotation from a former spouse stirs strong feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite people is to stir them up and arouse strong feelings in them.

clue.text: Odd sock's potential cause of merriment

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or peculiar
to sock someone is to punch them

explanation.surface: A mismatched item of hosiery might set people laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sock' looks like hosiery but is the verb meaning hit; the 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl of spiced alcoholic drink at a party can well lead to laughter and high spirits.

clue.text: Putin, say, has to defeat revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary means the letters are overturned into a new order

explanation.surface: The Russian leader must beat a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a noun, a rebel, but is the anagram signal; 'say' marks Putin as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Putin, as Russian president, is an example of a national leader.

clue.text: Roofing material for brood on top of tree

indicators.note: on here means placed after, so the brood piece follows the letter from tree
the top of a word in an across clue is its first letter

parts.note: a brood of chicks is a hatch

explanation.surface: Nesting material for chicks sitting at the top of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw or reeds laid on a cottage roof are the classic roofing material of rural England.

clue.text: Just loud music

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
an air is a tune, a piece of music

explanation.surface: Nothing but noisy tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' reads as 'only' but is the adjective meaning fair-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: A just ruling is an equitable, impartial one, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Open popular castle regularly occupied by herald

indicators.note: occupied by means the herald sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of castle, the even ones

parts.note: to herald is to foretell, which is to augur

explanation.surface: A well-liked fortress is taken over by a royal messenger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' is a verb here, to open formally; 'regularly' takes the even letters of castle, and 'occupied by' sets the herald between the popular word and those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To open a building or event formally is to inaugurate it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Unhappy and confused client, so sad, accepts ring

indicators.note: accepts means the jumble takes another letter inside it
confused tells us the letters of the three words are jumbled

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A customer, very sad and muddled, takes hold of a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' jumbles the eleven letters of the three words, and 'accepts' sets the ring letter among them; 'and' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone disconsolate is downcast and beyond comfort, so deeply unhappy.

clue.text: Muses get a Stoic in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble means the letters are in disorder

explanation.surface: Poetic goddesses cause problems for a philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muses' looks like the goddesses but is the verb meaning ponders.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to think deeply, a synonym of the verb meaning to ponder.

clue.text: Attempt to underpin flower business

indicators.note: to underpin is to sit beneath, so this piece comes below the other in a down answer

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Indus
an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: Trying to support a flowering commercial venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a crossword favourite for a river: something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry is commercial or manufacturing activity, the world of business.

clue.text: A barrier for good girl securing broadcast?

parts.note: a lass is a girl

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is heard rather than read, so its spoken form is used

parts.note: securing an envelope is sealing it

explanation.surface: A virtuous young woman bars transmission.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the invisible obstacle that stops women or minorities rising to top jobs.

clue.text: Graduate students supporting a learner with sign of hesitation

indicators.note: supporting means coming below the other pieces in a down answer

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plates on a learner driver's car
um is the sound of hesitating
NUS is the National Union of Students in Britain

explanation.surface: A former student union backing a hesitant learner.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumnus is a former pupil or graduate of a school or college.

clue.text: Call sir?

parts.note: to call someone sir is to give them a title, as when knighted

explanation.definitionFit: To entitle is to give a name or honorific, so addressing a knight as sir does exactly this.

clue.text: Challenged proof of title to cover Grand Prix racing

indicators.note: to cover means the deed wraps round the racing letters

parts.note: a deed is a legal document proving ownership
Formula One, F1, is Grand Prix racing, with the digit 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A racing driver's ownership papers are disputed.
explanation.definitionFit: To have defied someone is to have challenged or resisted their authority.

clue.text: Where a sommelier might be cooking tuna rarest

indicators.note: cooking means the letters of the following words are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A wine waiter at work while very rare tuna is being prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine waiter is employed in a dining establishment, so the definition describes its location.

clue.text: Policeman embracing universal success

indicators.note: embracing means the policeman's letters wrap round another

parts.note: a cop is a policeman
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: An officer hugs everyone and triumphs.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup is a brilliant stroke or notable triumph.

clue.text: Space traveller finds the compiler in bed!

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
the setter refers to themself, so the compiler is me

explanation.surface: An astronaut discovers the crossword setter asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet travels through space on its long orbit around the sun.

clue.text: Stung by scrap — then dismissing hospital

parts.note: a scrap is a bit, a small piece

indicators.note: dismissing means the word then loses one of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone stung by a quarrel is then discharged from hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' suggests a fight but means a small piece; 'dismissing' takes H out of THEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bitten by an insect is the same as being stung by it.

clue.text: Rough cost of redeveloping site with partner

indicators.note: redeveloping means the letters of site are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: A builder quotes a rough price for rebuilding a plot with a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: An approximate figure for a price is a synonym for a guess of the cost.

clue.text: Fail to embrace South American neglect

indicators.note: to embrace means the first word's letters go around the others

parts.note: an engine that fails dies
S is the compass abbreviation for South
US means American, as in US citizen

explanation.surface: Failing to welcome a South American shows neglect.
explanation.definitionFit: Disuse is the state of being neglected or no longer used.

clue.text: Watch nurse have a go

parts.note: SEN is State Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: A nurse keeping watch decides to have a go.
explanation.walkthrough: SEN, a State Enrolled Nurse, was a second-level nursing qualification in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is a guard on duty, so the definition is a synonym for a guard posted at a gate.
